build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: A market phase lets the player buy and sell goods at a town with visible prices, current money, cargo hold contents, and remaining capacity. Buying deducts money and adds cargo; selling adds money and removes cargo. Score 0 if no buying/selling exists or if transactions have no effect on state.

Route planning lets the player choose a destination and path with visible differences in cost, distance, hazard level, or expected profit. The choice commits the caravan to travel and determines what events may occur. Score 0 if travel is a single automatic button with no route choice.

Travel events such as bandits, storms, tolls, spoilage, shortcuts, or merchant encounters occur during transit and visibly alter cargo, money, time, or risk. The player sees the event and its consequence before arriving. Score 0 if no events occur during travel.

An upgrade system lets the player spend money on improvements — extra carts, guards, cold storage, scouts, permits, or better animals — that change future travel capacity, hazard mitigation, or market access. Upgrades persist across trips. Score 0 if no upgrades exist.

The full loop connects without restarting: title -> town market -> route choice -> travel/events -> arrival/sale -> next turn, cycling until a profit goal triggers success or debt triggers failure. Both end states are reachable and navigable. Score 0 if any transition is broken or the loop cannot complete.

The trade network contains multiple towns with distinct price profiles — at least four towns where goods have meaningfully different buy/sell values, creating arbitrage opportunities the player can discover. Score 0 if there is only one town or all towns have identical prices.

The cargo catalogue offers variety — at least five distinct goods or cargo types with different price spreads, weight, perishability, or risk profiles that create real loading decisions. Score 0 if there is only one tradeable good.
Market conditions shift over time — prices change between visits due to demand, scarcity, seasons, events, or player actions, so the optimal trade route is not static. Score 0 if prices never change.

Progression unlocks new content as the caravan grows — new towns on the map, higher-value contracts, riskier routes, premium goods, or advanced upgrades that were previously unavailable. Score 0 if the full game state is available from the start with no growth.

Travel events have variety — at least four distinct event types (bandits, weather, tolls, breakdowns, merchant encounters, shortcuts) with different consequences, so repeated trips do not feel identical. Score 0 if only one event type exists or events never occur.

The map, route lines, town locations, caravan position, and destination options are readable at 1280x720 without overlap. The player can parse where they are, where they can go, and what each route costs at a glance. Score 0 if route information is unreadable or hidden.

Market prices, money, cargo contents, capacity, and town demand are displayed clearly enough for the player to make informed buy/sell decisions without guessing. Score 0 if economic information is missing or unreadable.

Player actions produce visible feedback: buying/selling updates cargo and money displays, route selection highlights the chosen path, travel shows the caravan moving or progressing, and events show their consequence on state. Score 0 if actions happen silently with no visual response.

The flow connects title screen to gameplay to result screen without dead ends. The player can navigate from market to route to travel to next town without getting stuck or needing to restart. Score 0 if transitions are broken or missing.

Overall art coherence: map, towns, wagon, cargo, route lines, event cards, and UI belong to a consistent merchant/caravan visual language with a unified palette and style. The screen reads as a trade game, not a spreadsheet. Score 0 if the screen mixes incompatible styles or relies on unthemed placeholder rectangles for primary elements. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

The map feels authored and geographic — towns have distinct markers or crests, roads have character, terrain is suggested, and the trade network reads as a place rather than a graph diagram. Score 0 if the map is only a table of text or bare nodes and lines.

Cargo, upgrades, and goods are represented with icons, tokens, or illustrated pieces that have distinct silhouettes — the player can tell spices from timber from cloth at a glance. Score 0 if cargo identity is text-only.

HUD and UI panels use styled widgets — framed panels, icon-backed readouts, themed buttons, or parchment/merchant styling — not raw unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults. Numeric text uses a custom or styled font. Score 0 if primary UI elements are obviously unstyled default default widgets.

Motion and atmosphere: the caravan moves along routes with animation, market transactions have visual flourish, events appear with card or popup animation, and the map carries ambient life (swaying trees, flickering torches, drifting clouds). Score 0 if all state changes snap instantly with no animation.
